newsitem.title: USA: Highlights of NYS Gov's new tax-cutting program.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of NYS Gov's new tax-cutting program.

text.p: New York State Gov George Pataki, who has been announcing big tax cuts ahead of his fiscal 1998 budget, which is due Tuesday, on Friday called for over $1 billion of tax relief for cities, towns and counties.

The Republican governor also has said he would propose property tax relief, expected to cost the state hundreds of millions of dollars, as well as eliminating most estate and gift taxes, a move anticipated to cost about $400 million.

Pataki's latest proposal, which is expected to be followed by as many as two more initiatives that might be unveiled this weekend, competes with some tax reductions offered by the Democrat Assembly Leader, who is considering sales tax cuts, and the Republican Senate Majority Leader, who has proposed a four-year, $2.1 billion program of tax cuts.

"As a former mayor, I know firsthand the importance of freeing our cities, towns and counties from the heavy hand of state government," Pataki said, in prepared remarks. "By returning billions of dollars to local governments, we have given them the power to make their communities prosper and flourish once again."
The highlights of the Republican governor's latest initiative follows.
--Constituional amendment provision to prevent the state from forcing localities to pay for unfunded programs.

--Continue more than $700 million in unrestricted state aid to city governments, including over $114 million for New York City in the Stock Incentive Aid, which partly reimburses the city for the loss of stock transfer tax revenues.
--Reforming the Wicks Law to exempt local building projects that exceed $1 million, $2 million and in New York City only, $5 million, depending on how populous a municipality is.
The Wicks Law now requires local governments to use multiple contracts for a single building project, which Pataki said local estimates showed could boost costs unecessarily by 15 to 30 percent.
--Conform public requirements for absestos removal to non-governmental building standards. Pataki said current law imposes "unecessarily rigorous" standards on local governments.

--Require arbitrators in binding arbitration to place a priority on a municipality's ability to pay. Current law requires them to consider factors such as past contracts, settlements in comparable communities, and the ability of the public employer to pay.
--Limit municipal pension raises for firefighters, like an existing cap for police.
--Provide a $25 million Tax Stabliziation Fund for local governments to aid distressed localities and help them control property taxes.
--Provide for 15 upstate cities to again get nearly $49.3 million in Additional Emergency Financial Assistance to Eligible Municipalities.

--Strengthen oversight over distressed municipalities, and restructure the Municipal Bond Bank Agency to provide low-cost financing for distressed municipalities, which could securitize delinquent tax liens through a private trust.
